I cloned both repos and verified commit `816628b7` on `pron-lora-prep` directly (diff, not just the message — the report text from these sessions keeps not surviving, so I don't trust the commit message alone). Here's the honest state:

## Gap 1 — reciter classification: **resolved, and resolved well**

The agent's diff to `scripts/audio_audit.py` now documents the check explicitly: it looked at `_catalog.json`, `_registry/registry.json`, `_registry/registry_history/*.json`, and all 31 `_metadata/*/reciter.json` files, and confirmed **no style/type/category field exists anywhere**, and every `note` field is empty. That's stated in both a code comment and a new `style_metadata_note` key written into `reciter_audit.json` itself — so this time the finding is baked into a file, not just prose.

Given no such field exists, it added a curated `KNOWN_MURATTAL` set (26 dirs) used as a fallback after the literal name-match, tagged with a new `classification_source` field (`name-keyword` / `common-knowledge` / `none`). Result:

| classification | source | count |
|---|---|---|
| Murattal | name-keyword | 2 |
| Muallim | name-keyword | 1 |
| Mujawwad | name-keyword | 2 |
| Murattal | common-knowledge | 26 |
| unknown | none | 1 (`warsh`, already excluded) |

All the names you flagged for sanity-checking landed correctly: **Sudais, Shuraim, Hudhaify, Ayyoub, Basfar** are all in the `common-knowledge` Murattal set. 32/32 dirs now have a definite classification (only `warsh` stays `unknown`, which doesn't matter since it's excluded anyway for riwaya reasons). I ran the test suite locally — **112 tests still pass**, unchanged from session 3, consistent with this being a metadata-only tweak.

One honest caveat worth flagging back to you: this isn't independent verification — it's the agent's own knowledge asserting these are Murattal, same epistemic status as your own sanity check, just extended to 26 names instead of 5. It's a reasonable, well-documented default, not a hard fact pulled from data.

## Gap 2 — duration/sample-rate/channel numbers: **not addressed**

The commit touches exactly two files: `audio_audit.py` and `reciter_audit.json`. No ffprobe output, no scratch-download mention, no new script, nothing in the diff or commit message. This isn't "the report didn't survive the push" like the last two times — there's **no trace the work happened at all**. Third session in a row this specific ask has gone missing.

## Updating claude_context.md

I'll fold Gap 1's resolution in and sharpen the Gap 2 note (since "written report lost" is no longer the right diagnosis — it's now "possibly never attempted"). I can't push to your repo from here (no write credentials), so here's the replacement text for the two relevant paragraphs under "Session 3 result" — swap them in yourself:

a docstring). All 32 dirs now classified: name-keyword match first, else a
curated 26-name common-knowledge Murattal fallback (classification_source
field distinguishes the two). Sudais/Shuraim/Hudhaify/Ayyoub/Basfar all
landed Murattal as expected. Only warsh stays unknown (already excluded).
112 tests still pass.

**Gap 2 — still open, escalate:** duration/sample-rate/channel numbers for
the 6 shortlisted mp3s (Part C step 8) are missing a third session running.
Unlike sessions 2-3, this time there's no trace of the work in the diff at

prompt to the agent should require the 6 numbers be written into a small
committed file (e.g. data/pron/ffprobe_scratch.json), not just stated in the
chat reply, since plain-text replies are the thing that keeps failing.

Useful to separate what "scale" actually means here, because two different things got bundled under that word originally, and one of them has already been settled by accident.

**What's already locked in, whether you decide "small" or "big":** the 40-ayah shortlist (25 short + 15 medium) was built with a letter-coverage quota — ح, خ, ض each appear in exactly 16 ayat (24, 23, 25 occurrences), ع dominates naturally at 34/40 ayat since it's just more frequent in the language. Captions and dual-script JSONL are already done for all 40. That work is sunk cost regardless of what we pick next.

**The actual open question isn't really "10-20 vs 40 ayat" anymore.** My original session-1 proposal (10-20 ayat) predates this careful 40-ayat quota build. Cutting back down to 20 now would mean re-opening a problem that's already solved well — with only 16 ayat carrying ح/خ/ض in the first place, a further subset risks dropping below usable coverage for the rarer letters unless it's re-quota'd from scratch, which is real extra work for no clear benefit. The 40-set is already small — a handful of seconds each, trivial to download, and even at 3 reciters × 40 ayat × 2 scripts (dual-script pairing) that's ~240 training pairs, still tiny next to a full song-based LoRA run.

So I think the honest framing of "scale" left is really **two separate, smaller levers**, not one big one:

1. **How many reciters** — 2 vs 3 (you're already thinking this through separately).
2. **Whether to split "does the pipeline even work" from "does the pilot's science work."** i.e., run one throwaway tiny slice (8-10 ayat, no letter-coverage discipline needed) purely to shake out training/merge-tool bugs cheaply, *before* spending the full 40×N run — versus just going straight for the full 40×N as the pilot itself, since 40×N is still cheap in absolute terms.

Can I ask — when you said you wanted to think it through, was the worry more about **total training compute/time**, about **not wanting to over-commit before knowing the approach works at all**, or something else? That'll tell me which of these two levers is actually the one worth deciding now.
